title: Born in the USA: Finding regional identity in American single malt whiskey
summary: This blossoming whiskey category is already showing local character. Susannah Skiver Barton explores how regionality is shaping American single malts, with a region-by-region guide – and six great bottles to try.
content: <p>A veteran journalist and seasoned critic, Susannah Skiver Barton writes about whisky and spirits from around the world. Bylines include <em>The New York Times</em>, <em>Bon Appétit</em>, <em>Imbibe</em>, <em>Food &amp; Wine</em>, <em>Whisky Magazine</em>, <em>VinePair</em>, <em>PUNCH</em>, and more. She is a Certified Spirits Specialist and recipient of the 2020 Alan Lodge Young International Drinks Writer Award. More at <a href="http://susannahskiverbarton.com/" target="_blank">susannahskiverbarton.com</a>.</p>

content: <div class="author-description"><p>Claire joined <em>Decanter</em> in 2024 with wide-ranging experience in the wine industry including auction, winemaking, communications and journalism. She holds the WSET Diploma in addition to the Italian Wine Scholar Guild and Vinitaly International Academy Wine Ambassador certifications. She enjoys hemisphere hopping: with two vintages under her belt in both Australia’s Yarra Valley and Vittoria in south-eastern Sicily. As Special Projects Editor at <em>Decanter</em>, Claire oversees all commercial content and bespoke projects. A qualified interpreter, she speaks fluent Italian and French and is working on her Spanish, Romanian and German.</p></div>

title: New Château Margaux MD Aurélien Valance on key challenges and the wine that started it all
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Chris Mercer is a Bristol-based freelance editor and journalist who spent nearly four years as digital editor of <strong>Decanter.com</strong>, having previously been <em>Decanter’s</em> news editor across online and print.</p><p>He has written about, and reported on, the wine and food sectors for more than 10 years for both consumer and trade media.</p><p>Chris first became interested in the wine world while living in Languedoc-Roussillon after completing a journalism Masters in the UK. These days, his love of wine commonly tests his budgeting skills.</p><p>Beyond wine, Chris also has an MSc in food policy and has a particular interest in sustainability issues. He has also been a food judge at the UK’s Great Taste Awards.</p></div>

summary: The grape that knows no borders...
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Magdalena is a Niagara-based international wine, gastronomy and travel freelancer with over 40 years experience in Canadian wine. Over the past 16 years, she has played a pivotal role in elevating the global presence for Ontario wine and recognition as a premier destination. Certified by WSET and the Global Sustainable Tourism Council, she champions sustainable practices and wines that reflect a sense of place. A Decanter World Wine Awards judge and Canada’s Regional Ambassador for the Old Vines Conference, she travels widely to explore and taste wine from all regions. She has a particular interest in the complexities of skin-fermented whites. Her micro-sized @TinyBatchWine project, where she makes magnums of Gamay and Skin Fermented Gewürztraminer, honors her late father’s winemaking legacy.</p></div>
